ai.description: The Kachh gecko reaches 50 mm in snout-vent length. It is greyish-brown with dark transverse bands and possesses enlarged, trihedral tubercles on the dorsal surface and a slender, tapering tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Kachh Gecko is best distinguished by the presence of 12–14 longitudinal rows of enlarged, trihedral tubercles on its back, which are notably larger than the interspaces.
ai.habitat: The Kachh Gecko inhabits arid, rocky scrublands and boulder-strewn hills in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate elevations in dry, sparse vegetation.
ai.behavior: The Kachh gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects and arthropods among rocky crevices and arid landscapes.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Kachh Gecko is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, generally between April and June.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtopodion kachhense* is endemic to the arid regions of Gujarat and Rajasthan in northwestern India, typically inhabiting rocky outcrops at low elevations.
